visuals.title: Where TB can go
visuals.text: Lungs most often; extrapulmonary sites are the spine (Pott's), lymph nodes, meninges, ileocaecal bowel and skin (lupus vulgaris).

glossary.Granulomatous infection: An infection the body walls off with granulomas, clusters of macrophages and lymphocytes.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Weakened immune defences, from disease such as HIV or from drugs.
glossary.Endemic area: A region where a disease is constantly present in the population.
glossary.Immunosuppressive therapy: Drugs that damp down the immune system, such as steroids or biologics.
glossary.Pulmonary TB: Tuberculosis of the lungs, the infectious form.
glossary.Night sweats: Drenching sweating during sleep, often a sign of infection, TB or lymphoma.
glossary.Crackles: Fine popping sounds on auscultation from fluid or opening of small airways.
glossary.Auscultation: Listening to the body, usually with a stethoscope.
glossary.Extrapulmonary TB: TB outside the lungs, such as lymph nodes, bone, gut or meninges.
glossary.GI TB: Tuberculosis of the gut, usually the ileocaecal region.
glossary.Skeletal TB: TB of bones and joints, most often the spine.
glossary.Papules: Small raised solid skin bumps under 1 cm.
glossary.Nodules: Raised solid skin lumps over 1 cm.
glossary.TB meningitis: TB infection of the meninges, with a subacute onset over days to weeks.
glossary.Subacute: Developing over days to weeks, between acute and chronic.
glossary.Mycobacterial culture: Growing mycobacteria from a sample in the lab; takes weeks but is the most sensitive test.
glossary.Sputum: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.
glossary.Fibronodular opacification: Areas of scarring and small nodules seen as white shadows on a chest X-ray.
glossary.Upper zones: The top third of each lung field on a chest X-ray.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes, a blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Tuberculin skin test: Another name for the Mantoux test: tuberculin injected into the skin and induration measured.
glossary.Quadruple therapy: Four drugs taken together; here the RIPE regimen.
glossary.Rifamycins: The antibiotic family that includes rifampicin and rifabutin.
glossary.Gout: Painful joint inflammation from urate crystals.
glossary.Optic atrophy: Wasting of the optic nerve, causing loss of vision.
glossary.Parenteral: Given by a route other than the gut, such as injection.
glossary.Colour blindness: Difficulty telling colours apart; with ethambutol, red-green first.
glossary.Laryngeal TB: TB of the larynx, highly infectious.
glossary.Live vaccine: A vaccine containing a weakened living organism, unsafe in immunosuppression.
glossary.Intracellular organism: A microbe that lives and multiplies inside host cells.
glossary.Macrophages: Immune cells that engulf and digest microbes and debris.
glossary.Oxygen tension: The partial pressure of oxygen in a tissue.
glossary.Haematogenous dissemination: Spread of infection through the bloodstream.
glossary.Lymphatic spread: Spread of infection through lymph vessels to lymph nodes.
glossary.RNA polymerase: The enzyme that copies DNA into RNA.
glossary.Dormant: Alive but inactive and not multiplying.
